title: A body without a soul: the vessel exists on its own, the kavana goes to it, and the light follows
overview:
Chapter 30 explains why, when the light leaves, the vessels remain "like a body without a soul". If a vessel were only light grown thick, nothing would be left. But the root of the vessels comes first, so a vessel exists on its own, like an empty balloon, and that is what *ihu v'garmohi chad* means.

So the *kavana* in a Name goes to the source of its vessel, as saying a friend's name means the friend himself, and the light follows by itself. Even the *Arizal*'s *kavanos* on the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* are no *avoda zara*: a fundraiser appeals to a man's kindness and means the man. The class ends on three prayers, of Moshe, of David and of the poor man, and the poor man's works best.

Every vessel has three levels, inner, middle and outer: thought, speech and action; in the heart, its two chambers and the lungs; in the liver, the trace of life left in sleep, the pulse and the body's energy; in a *mitzva*, *kavana*, feeling and deed. The vessel is the main thing, and without the light it is good for nothing.

terms.gloss: vessels: organs, not containers; they exist on their own, and without the light they are good for nothing

sections.title: A body without a soul: the vessels have an existence of their own
sections.summary: If a vessel were only the light grown thick, nothing would be left when the light goes. But the root of the vessels comes before the root of the lights, so the vessel exists on its own, like an empty balloon, and that vessel is what *ihu v'garmohi chad* speaks of.

phrases.he: (ל) ובזה יובן המאמר וכד אנת תסתלק מנייהו
אשתארו כו' כגופא בלא נשמתא
phrases.en: all the names remained like a body without a soul

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הכלים דמוחא ולבא כו' שנקרא גופא בלא נשמתא
שהן בחינת האורות דנר''נ כו'
אך מאין ימצא מציאת כלי בלא אור, מאחר שמהתעבות האור נעשה כלי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: If the *kli* comes from this *ibbui* of the light, so when the lights leave, there would be no *kli* at all left.

blocks.text: When You withdraw, **all the names remained like a body without a soul**: the body is the *kelim* (vessels) of *mocha* and *liba*, brain and heart; the soul, the lights. But if the *kli* comes from the *hisabus* (thickening) of the light, why is anything left when the lights leave?

phrases.he: אבל לפי הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: like what we said before

phrases.he: דשרש הכלים קדם לשרש האורות כו',
אם כן יש מציאות לכלים בפני עצמם,
phrases.en: Really, the *kli* does have a *metzius* of itself.

phrases.he: ועל זה אמר דאיהו וגרמוהי חד כו'
phrases.en: That's what it meant when it says *ihu v'garmohi chad*.

blocks.text: But, **like what we said before** with the balloon, the root of the vessels comes first: **Really, the *kli* does have a *metzius* of itself**, though alone it is an uninflated balloon. *Ihu v'garmohi chad* (He and His vessels are one) means this *kli*, not vessels of thickened light.

sections.title: Intending the Name: aim at the source of the vessel, and the light follows
sections.summary: The *kavana* in a Name goes to the source of its vessel, the One whose name it is, as a name means the person himself; then the light comes by itself. Even the Kabbalists' *kavanos* on the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* aim at Him, as a fundraiser aims at a man's kindness and means the man.

phrases.he: (ולפי זה המכוין בשם יהו״ה,
כמו בח''י ברכאן דצלותא,
phrases.en: like in the *Shemoneh Esrei*

phrases.he: יכוין למקור התהוות הכלי,
phrases.en: The *kavana* is to the *makor* of the *his'havus*: not to the light, but to the *Atzmus*, which is the *makor* of the *his'havus* of the *kli*.

phrases.he: שהוא עיקר בחינת השם,
phrases.en: That's the main thing of the *shem*.

phrases.he: דאיהו וגרמוהי חד כו'
phrases.en: him and his name is one thing: you don't mean the name, you actually mean him.

blocks.text: Aiming at the Name *Havaya*, as in the *Shemoneh Esrei*, one aims at the *makor* (source) of the vessel's coming into being: **not to the light, but to the *Atzmus***. That is the main thing of the *shem* (name).

blocks.title: A friend we all know
blocks.text: So with a friend we all know: the *kavana* (intention) is not on his light, the knowledge of who he is, but *mamash* on him. *Ihu v'garmohi chad*: **you don't mean the name, you actually mean him**.

phrases.he: וממילא נמשך האור אחר הכלי,
phrases.en: And once you have the *kli*, the light comes automatically.

phrases.he: כי דרכו של איש כו' ודי למבין).
phrases.en: Because the man runs after the woman.

blocks.text: **And once you have the *kli*, the light comes automatically.** Aim at the friend himself and everything comes with it: how he looks, his smile, his brain, his character, his height. Aim at the *etzem* (essence) and all the *giluyim* (revelations) come.

blocks.question: When we write "Hashem" in place of His Name we also mean the Aibershter. Why may we write that, and not other names?
blocks.text: As with writing G-d with a dash: the name written is not really the name, and you mean the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d). Writing "Hashem", you really think of the four letters of *Havaya*.

"Hashem", "the Name", is like a nickname: aimed at a person but not *mamash* at him. Really one should not even write it; the *Aibershter* permitted it, since anything else would also be a *kinui* (a by-name), as even the four letters said out are.

They reach Him in the end, but not the *etzem* directly. There is an upper, actual *Havaya* (its *yud* *Atzilus*, the other letters *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, the thorn of the *yud* *Keser*), and above it the divine letters the Name comes from: what the Kabbalistic *kavanos* of the *Shemoneh Esrei* aim at, each Name with its *milui* (spelling out) and vowel points.

That is the cat inside the cat: a *Havaya* above *Atzilus* and its source, the *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN* of *Adam Kadmon*, Names with mathematical things and very deep *kavanos* that the Kabbalists aim at. Ours is not that: we write "G-d" and mean the *Aibershter*; the *Arizal* aimed at actual levels and knew what they were.

blocks.title: The Kohen Gadol who said a Name and went up
blocks.text: The sages of the Mishna, saying a Name, would go to that world: in the story of the Ten Martyrs, the *Kohen Gadol* said a Name and went upstairs. Their *kavanos* aimed at the actual names of actual entities.

So is it not *avoda zara* (idol worship) to aim at the outer names of the vessels of *Zeir Anpin*? A Kabbalistic prayer book gives each Name its *milui* and vowel points (*patach* is *chesed* and *kamatz* *gevura*, he thinks, not remembering it all), a different *Havaya* for each blessing; asking for money, you aim at a certain *sefira*. It sounds like worshipping stars and constellations on a higher level: praying to the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.question: Then aim higher, at the vessels of Adam Kadmon or at the Names in the Kav. Is that not avoda zara too?
blocks.text: No: you aim at the inner side of those Names, the outer vessels of *Adam Kadmon*, whose inner vessels are the outer vessels of the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought); higher, at the Names in the *Kav*, already pure G-dliness, the *tiferes* of the *Ein Sof*. Still a *sefira*? It does not matter: really you aim at how it is in the *Atzmus*, not at the *sefira*.

blocks.title: Aiming at your ear
blocks.text: He is aiming at the listener's ear right now: not too loud, not too quiet. Not talking to the ear, he aims at it, and the ear is connected to the person. For help he aims at the *midda* (attribute) of *chesed*, with a tearjerker about the little kids with patches on their yarmulkes; to get him to come beat up a guy, at his *gevura*: what that guy said about your mama. Explaining, he aims his whole voice at the listener's *bina*, and through it his *chachma*.

blocks.title: Talking to a friend's kindness
blocks.text: Heart, anger or kindness, he is appealing to the person. Suppose he came home and was asked whom he had talked to, and said: to a friend's kindness; to the outer vessels of *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus* of him, for a person is a whole world. That's where his *kavanos* were, telling him about the kids with the patches. Anybody would tell him he's a nut. Why? Because, though he did aim there, he was really aiming at the only one who can put his hand in his pocket and write a check for these poor kids: the friend himself. He was talking to him all along.

sensitivity.reason: "A nut", said of himself in the story.

blocks.text: So too now: he aims at *bina* of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus* of the listener, and not even that. First the ear, the outer vessel of *bina*, *bina* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*; then the *bina* of the brain and of the soul, which gives the body its life; and really not *bina* at all, but the person himself.

That is the text: aim at the outer vessels of *chesed*, and the light of *chesed* comes by itself and gets him to give the donation for better yarmulkes. He aims at the vessels, not the light, **because the man runs after the woman**.

As for the vowel points: *kamatz* is *Keser*, *patach* *chachma*, *tzeirei* *bina*, *segol* *chesed* or *daas*, *sheva* *gevura*, *cholam* *tiferes*, *chirik* *netzach*, *shuruk* *hod*, *kubutz* *yesod*, and *Malchus* has no vowel point at all.

blocks.question: A listener had seen from the Rebbe something different: kamatz is gevura and patach is chesed. Which is it?
blocks.text: Could be; there are different systems. *Kamatz* is a fist, closing, *tzimtzum*; *patach* is open; and it can apply differently in different places.

blocks.question: We pray that our prayer be like that of an old man whose beard is grown and whose peyos are beautiful. If you pray from the heart, fine; if not, what difference does it make that you know all the right words?
blocks.text: The vowels do not matter here: these *kavanos* aim upstairs at the outer *middos*, as one aims at a person's. One fundraiser doesn't know you and makes a general *kavana* of schmaltz; another knows the names of your outer vessels, which buttons to press, and does better. A regular guy davens in general; the *Arizal* knew exactly how to approach the *Aibershter*.

That makes sense, but it leaves us kind of weak: your prayer is not the *Arizal*'s, who knew the *Aibershter* the way that fundraiser knows how to kvetch the money out of you. That is why one goes to a *Rebbe*, and why, with a problem with the rain, they went to Choni HaMe'agel or the Rashbi: his prayer went to the right place.

blocks.title: Three prayers: of Moshe, of David, of the poor man
blocks.text: But three kinds are named: a "prayer of Moshe", a "prayer of David" and a "prayer of the poor man, when he is faint and pours out his speech before G-d". A prayer of Moshe is a big *tzaddik* coming: you don't say no, even if he can't talk well.

blocks.title: Zaltsman on Yom Kippur
blocks.text: A prayer of David, the sweet singer of Israel, who knew the right words and melodies: like when Zaltsman, a great cantor, sang on Yom Kippur, and people who never gave any money pledged ten thousand dollars, crying, remembering their mother and father and grandfather, their grandmother's wig, the cholent they used to eat.

The *tefilla l'ani*, the prayer of the poor man, is bringing the kid himself, patches and all: "I'm not a fundraiser and not a *tzaddik*, but here's the kid." A prayer of Moshe needs a *tzaddik* like Moshe; one of David, all the songs, upstairs the letters, vowel points, cantillation, crowns and tags: by the *Arizal*, singing as they sing upstairs.

So what do you do? There is always a *tefilla l'ani*. It is so good that even King David said, "For I am poor and needy": he could have come with a prayer of David, and he came with the prayer of the poor man. When you see the kid with the patches on the yarmulke, that works best to bring out the *midda* of *chesed*. The same with the other *middos*: to bring out a man's *gevura*, show him the graffiti with "yo mama" written on it, or his busted window. Nothing works better than that.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 045 opens by finishing class 044's teaching on the three prayers, before it rereads the end of line 7 (w327).

sensitivity.reason: The "yo mama" graffiti as the example of what provokes anger.
sensitivity.publishable: So what do you do? There is always a *tefilla l'ani*. It is so good that even King David said, "For I am poor and needy": he could have come with a prayer of David, and he came with the prayer of the poor man. When you see the kid with the patches on the yarmulke, that works best to bring out the *midda* of *chesed*. The same with the other *middos*: to bring out a man's *gevura*, show him the graffiti on his wall, or his busted window. Nothing works better than that.

blocks.text: The catch: you have to be an *ani* and know that you really have nothing. Everybody is one (if King David was, what are we?), but without knowing it you lack an *ani*'s tears. A poor man who comes as a Moshe gets thrown out; one who can't sing and plays David hears "You're hurting my ears." He must come as an *ani*.

sections.title: Three levels in every vessel: inner, middle and outer, as thought, speech and action
sections.summary: Vessels are inner, middle and outer, for the *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi* of the light, and most of the hiding is in the outer. In a *midda* like *chesed* they are the letters of thought, speech and action; but those letters are only garments, and the true vessels of the soul are the brain and the heart.

phrases.he: והנה יש ג' מדריגות בכלים, פנימים ואמצעים וחיצוניות.
והענין ידוע
phrases.en: And it's a known thing

phrases.he: כי לנגד ט׳ ספירות חב''ד חג''ת נה''י, יש ג' מיני כלים פנימית הכלים הוא בחינת הגבלת האור דחב''ד שבאור ואמצעות הכלים הגבלת חג''ת דאור, וחיצוניות הכלים הוא הגבלת נה''י דאור כו'
והיינו אתה סתר
phrases.en: You are hidden

phrases.he: למפרע דרת''ס,
phrases.en: That's the backward of *rosh, toch, sof*.

phrases.he: שעיקר ההגבלה וההסתר בחיצוניות הכלים כו'
phrases.en: That's what you're seeing: you're seeing the *chitzoniyus hakelim*.

blocks.text: Now the vessels have three levels, inner, middle and outer: the *rosh, toch, sof* (head, middle, end) spoken of before. The inner limit the *Chabad* of the light, the middle its *Chagas*, the outer its *Nehi*.

*Ata seser*, **You are hidden**: **That's the backward of *rosh, toch, sof***. From outside the *samech* comes first, so it reads *seser*, hidden. The main hiding is in the outer vessels; past the *samech* is the *tav*, past that the inner vessels: all *seser*.

phrases.he: וגם בענין מה שיש בכלי בחינת השפעת וירידת השפע למקבל דוקא כנזכר לעיל, גם כן כלול מג' מדריגות פנימית הכלי הוא בחינת הבאת אור שפע דחב''ד ואמצעית להבאת והמשכת אור דחג''ת, וחיצוניות להבאת שפע דנה''י כו'
ועל דרך משל ט׳ ספירות שבאור מדת החסד, המוגבל בג' מיני אותיות אותיות המחשבה בחינת פנימית הכלי לחב''ד שבחסד

blocks.text: The vessel's giving has the same three levels, so *chesed* is bounded in three kinds of letters. Reaching for a friend's *chesed* from outside, it goes first to the letters of thought, the inner vessel, the *Chabad* of the *chesed*: he wants the friend to think about it.

phrases.he: ואותיות הדבור
phrases.en: And then it comes to when we're talking about it

phrases.he: אמצעית כלי לחג''ת שבחסד,
phrases.en: That's the middle *kli*, for *Chagas* of the *chesed*.

phrases.he: ואותיות המעשה לבחינת נה''י שבאור החסד שהוא בחינת כח המעשה שבחסד, לעשותו בפועל ממש יש לו כלי מיוחד,
ואהבה שבחסד
phrases.en: the actual feeling of the *chesed* in your heart

phrases.he: יש לו כלי מיוחד, ושכל וטעם שבחסד יש לו כלי מיוחד כו'
ועל הרוב,
phrases.en: And generally

phrases.he: השכל והטעם שבחסד מהרהר במחשבה,
והאהבה שבו יאמר בדיבור,
phrases.en: And general love, the emotion, is said in the words.

phrases.he: וכח המעשה שבו יעשה בפועל ממש

blocks.text: Speech is **the middle *kli*, for *Chagas* of the *chesed***; action is its *Nehi*, the *koach hamaaseh* (power to act), not the deed itself, which is *Malchus*.

Love (felt in the heart), reason (convincing a friend that a charity is good, so he thinks it over) and the power of action each have a vessel. Generally the reason is thought and the love spoken, though either can go either way; action does it in deed.

phrases.he: (אמנם כשבא בג' מיני אותיות דמחשבה דבור ומעשה נקרא לבושין
דמנהון כו'
phrases.en: From these *levushim* come the *neshamos* of people.

phrases.he: שלמטה מבחינת כלים דעליהם אמר איהו וגרמוהי חד כו', ולא על הלבושין אבל בחינת הכלים לנר''נ הוא מוחא ולבא כו'

blocks.text: In thought, speech and action they are *levushim* (garments): **from these *levushim* come the *neshamos* of people**. *Ihu v'garmohi chad* speaks of the vessels above them, not the garments: a *kli* is not a vessel but an organ.

The vessels of *NaRaN* are the brain and the heart: thought is in the mind, speech from the heart. How speech passes from the heart's *hevel* (breath) to the lungs, which push it, while the mouth cuts it into words, comes later.
So emotion is in speech: the more a person feels, the more he talks. A fundraiser who really feels for the little children speaks words that come from the heart.

sections.title: The heart: understanding, feeling, and the breath of the lungs
sections.summary: The heart has the three levels: the *Chabad* of a *midda* in its right chamber, the felt *midda* that beats in the left, and its outside, the breath of the lungs, which carries the *midda* into the blood. Anger shows in all three.

phrases.he: ובלב יש ג' מדריגות,
phrases.en: And in the heart, there's also three levels

phrases.he: פנימים ואמצעים וחיצוניות לנגד ט׳ ספירות כו' בחינת חב''ד שבמדת האהבה או היראה
כו' שנקרא מושכל של המדות
phrases.en: Which is the understanding of why the *midda* should be this *midda*

phrases.he: כו' הוא בחלל הימיני שבלב, שמאיר בו ממוח החכמה ששליט על הלב כו'

blocks.text: The heart too has three levels, each with three of its own. Its *Chabad*, the *muskal* (the understood) of the *middos*, is **the understanding of why the *midda* should be this *midda***: in the right chamber, lit by *chachma*, which rules the heart.

phrases.he: וחג''ת שבאהבה ויראה כו'
שהוא הנקרא מורגש
phrases.en: That means actual feeling of the emotion.

phrases.he: היינו בבחינת אמצעית כלי הלב, שהוא רוח החיים שדופק בחלל השמאלי שנמשך ממוח בינה שנקרא רוח והוא בחינת כלי הרגש החיות של המדות בהתפעלותם כו'

blocks.text: The *Chagas*, the felt, is the **actual feeling of the emotion**, beating in the left chamber, drawn from *bina*: angry, the heart beats and the breath comes faster.

phrases.he: וחיצוניות הלב הוא הבל החזה כו',
phrases.en: the lungs

phrases.he: ששם כלי הטבעת המדות כו'
phrases.en: That means he'll start breathing faster or slower.

phrases.he: שהוא לנגד בחינת נפש, בחינת נה''י שבמדות כו'
ומשם מאיר בנפש שבדם,
phrases.en: And from the *hadpaka* of the lungs, it'll go into the *nefesh* in the blood.

phrases.he: שהוא מרכבה לגבי רוח שבלב בכלל
phrases.en: Which that's the *merkava*, the chariot, for the *ruach* which is in the heart in general.

blocks.text: The outside of the heart, the *hevel hachazeh* (breath of the chest), is **the lungs**, where **he'll start breathing faster or slower** by the *midda*. This is *nefesh*, the *Nehi* of the *middos*.

From the lungs it enters the *nefesh* in the blood, with the whole crazy chemistry of breathing: panicked, a person hyperventilates and hormones go into his blood. So it lights up the *nefesh* in the blood, **the *merkava*, the chariot, for the *ruach* which is in the heart in general**.

sections.title: The liver: a trace of life in sleep, the pulse, and the energy of the body
sections.summary: The *nefesh* in the liver has three levels too: the *kista d'chayusa*, the trace of life left in sleep, where dreams come from; the arousal of the blood and the pulse; and the energy sent to all the limbs. In exile, which is sleep, only that trace is left, and the Jewish people are folded up like a fetus.

phrases.he: וגם בחינת נפש שבכבדא כלול מג' מדריגות, פנימי ואמצעי וחיצון כו'. פנימי הוא הנקרא בזוהר
קיסטא דחיותא
phrases.en: the *reshimu* of the life force

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת רשימו שנשאר מבחינת רוח בשעת השינה כו'
phrases.en: When he's sleeping, there's a *reshimu* left over from his spirit while he's sleeping.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת מוחין חב''ד דקטנות שבנפש כו'

blocks.text: The *nefesh* in the liver too has inner, middle and outer levels. He leaves out the brain, which also has three.

The inner, the *Zohar*'s *kista d'chayusa*, is **the *reshimu* of the life force** left from his spirit in sleep, the small *mochin* of *Chabad* in the *nefesh*. Dreams come from it, as will be explained: a trace of all his day's *mochin* and *inyanim*.

phrases.he: ואמצעי היינו התפעלות חיות גשמי של כח התנועה וההרגש שבדם, הוא הנפש, כמו בדפק שביד כו'

blocks.text: The middle is the physical arousal of movement and feeling in the blood, the pulse: excited, the heart beats and the blood circulates faster, and that lets him move (fear makes him run; a runner whose blood doesn't pump can't run long). The pulse means the whole circulation.

blocks.title: Two angry men and a candlelit dinner
blocks.text: Mad, his blood boils; relaxed, it slows. The arousal of the outer *middos* and the power of movement come from the blood pumping: without good circulation you can't join the marathon. Two guys getting angrier at each other jump up and down and can't stand still; an electrocardiogram would show the blood pumping. Or a guy relaxed at a candlelit dinner, overlooking the city from the mountains. Not the feeling but the arousal of life that goes with it is in the pulse, the rhythm of the blood: that's why rhythm music gets people jumping up and down.

phrases.he: והחיצון הוא בחינת נה''י שבכבד ששולח חיצוניות החיות בכל האברים והפנימית מבדיל כו' כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: The outer is the *Nehi* of the liver, sending life out to the limbs. So: inner, the *kista d'chayusa*, the *reshimu* of the *mochin* (of the anger, say) in the liver; middle, the blood pumping; outer, the energy reaching the body, energized when angry, de-energized and sleepy when relaxed. The liver divides between the two systems.
Back to "the inner divides": the main thing the liver does is to be a sieve, the intermediary between the heart and the guts, putting the whole thing together.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said at the end of class 045 (w2989), after line 61, when he goes back to line 41.

blocks.question: Where is the diaphragm, which separates the upper organs from the lower ones, in relation to the liver?
blocks.text: That is only a physical separation. The actual intermediary is the liver: the blood with the air in it, its cleaning, the bad stuff taken out and the good put in.
blocks.outOfPlace: At the end of class 045, on line 41.

blocks.text: A doctor he learned this with was amazed that it is really so: the liver, she said, is one of the most important organs, the one that puts the blood together. He is unsure of the details (it cleans the blood, he thinks; corpuscles come from the marrow), but joining the respiratory and digestive systems into one blood is the liver's work, the *memutza* (intermediary) between them.
blocks.outOfPlace: At the end of class 045, on line 41.

phrases.he: שבזמן הגלות שנקרא שינה, אין ההארה דמלכות דאצילות, בחינת נפש בעולמות דבי''ע, רק בחינת קיסטא דחיותא רשימו דבחינת רוח שבלב אדם העליון כו'

blocks.text: In exile, called sleep, the *nefesh*, the light of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* below, is absent; only the *kista d'chayusa*, the *reshimu* of the *ruach*, remains, as it alone keeps a sleeper alive.

phrases.he: וכנסת ישראל, שנמשלים לבחינת עיבור בגלות היינו כמו הולד שמקופל ראשו בין ברכיו כו',
תלת גו תלת כו'
phrases.en: Three inside of three, meaning *Chabad* inside of *Chagas* inside of *Nehi*.

phrases.he: שהמוחין חב''ד בהעלם בחג''ת וחג''ת בנה''י כו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר).

blocks.text: *Knesses Yisroel* (the community of Israel) in exile is likened to an *ibur* (a fetus), head folded between its knees: **Three inside of three, meaning *Chabad* inside of *Chagas* inside of *Nehi***. So people sleep curled like a fetus: *Chabad* hidden in *Chagas*, *Chagas* in *Nehi*, and only the *Nehi* keeping him alive.

sections.title: The 248 limbs of the King: kavana, feeling and deed in a mitzva
sections.summary: Each *mitzva* has the three vessels: the *kavana* inside, the love, fear and feeling in the middle, and the deed outside, like the marrow, sinews and flesh of an organ. Nine *sefiros* in nine, in three levels, make 243, and the five *chassadim hamagdilim*, the general will drawn through the *Kav* into every *mitzva*, make 248.

phrases.he: והנה בענין המצות שנקרא רמ''ח אברין דמלכא כידוע, הרי ג׳ פעמים ט׳ פעמים ט׳ בג' מיני מדריגות דראש תוך סוף שבכלים, כנזכר לעיל עולה רמ''ג וה' חסדים המגדילים, הן רמ''ח כו'

blocks.text: The *mitzvos* are the King's 248 limbs: three levels of vessels of nine *sefiros*, each in nine, make 243, and the five *chassadim hamagdilim* (the kindnesses that make grow), the spreading of life, make 248 (see *Torah Or*: Avram and Avraham).

phrases.he: ובחינת חב''ד היינו אור הכוונה שבמצות שיש לזה כלי פנימית מיוחד, ובהגבלה כו'
phrases.en: So in the *mitzvos*, the inner *kli* is the *kavana* of the *mitzva*.

phrases.he: ובחינת חג''ת, אהבה ויראה וביטול כו', יש לזה כלי אמצעי כו' ובחינת נה''י בחינת כח המעשה, לעשות רצון המלך בלבד כו', יש לזה כלי החיצוני (ובכלל היינו כונה וברכה ומעשה או יחוד ברכה וקדושה, שנקרא יב''ק כו'

blocks.text: **In the *mitzvos*, the inner *kli* is the *kavana* of the *mitzva***, its *Chabad*; its love, fear and *bittul* (self-nullification) have the middle vessel; the power to do the King's will, the outer. In general: *kavana*, blessing (the feeling) and deed; or *Yichud*, *Bracha*, *Kedusha*, *YaBaK*, as in crossing the river Yabbok.

phrases.he: שהוא ענין בשר וגידין ועצמות שבכל אבר כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.text: Flesh, sinews and bones: in every organ the flesh is the outer vessel, the sinews (nerves and blood vessels) the middle, and the bones the inner, the *mochin*: the brain is inside the bones, the marrow.

phrases.he: וה' חסדים המגדילים כו'
היינו בחינת כללות המשכת גלוי אור אלה״י שעל ידי כל מצוה
phrases.en: Meaning the *chassadim hamagdilim* of the *ratzon*.

phrases.he: על ידי המשכת הקו שממשיך למקור כל החסדים, דאיהו שקיו דאילנא כו',
phrases.en: Means the general *ratzon* that's in each *mitzva*.

phrases.he: וכמאמר אנת ממלא כל שמהן כו'
phrases.en: You fill up all the names.

blocks.text: The *chassadim hamagdilim* are the light each *mitzva* draws through the *Kav* from the source of all *chassadim*: **the general *ratzon* that's in each *mitzva***, as in **You fill up all the names**.

sections.title: Why "without a soul": the vessel is the main thing, and good for nothing without the light
sections.summary: The body is called a body without a soul because the vessels exist on their own, and still they need the light of the *Kav*. The *kavanos* are aimed at the vessels, but a vessel without light is a limp balloon, so the light is the main thing.

phrases.he: (ולפי זה מה שכתוב אשתאר כגופא כו',
phrases.en: This thing that it says, it remains like a body without a soul

phrases.he: משום דגם בחינת גופא בג' כלים הנזכר לעיל, צריך להארת אור אין סוף שבקו, שממלא כל שמהן
לפי שיש שרש להתהוות הכלים בפני עצמן כנזכר לעיל.
phrases.en: The *kelim* really have their own existence.

blocks.text: So **it remains like a body without a soul**: even the body, the vessels, needs the light of the *Ein Sof* in the *Kav*. The vessels have their own existence, but without light they are a dead body.

phrases.he: אך אם כן,
phrases.en: But if you say like that

phrases.he: למה תלה הדבר במה שאינו עיקר הדבר, שהוא מה שכתוב בלא נשמתא?
phrases.en: If the main thing is the *kelim*, so who cares about the *neshama*?

blocks.text: **But if you say like that**, why hang it on what is not the main thing? **If the main thing is the *kelim*, so who cares about the *neshama*?** That, he thinks, is the text's question.

phrases.he: אך להיות שעיקר הכלים הן לנגד ט׳ ספירות דנר''נ,
phrases.en: the whole *kelim* come *davka* from the *inyan* of the ten *sefiros* of *NaRaN*.

phrases.he: ובסיבת הגדלת האור יבא הגדלת הכלי,
phrases.en: It's only when you fill it up with light, then you have a properly working *kli*.

phrases.he: בשביל הבאת אור השפע למטה,
ואי אנת תסתלק כו'
phrases.en: If you go out of it

phrases.he: ישאר הכלי כגוף בלא נשמה, בלא התפשטות כלל ודי למבין):
phrases.en: It'll be like a limp balloon.

blocks.text: The vessels come *davka* from the ten *sefiros* of *NaRaN*; without light a *kli* is as useless as a tire without air. **It's only when you fill it up with light, then you have a properly working *kli***.

blocks.title: The empty balloon
blocks.text: The vessel brings the flow down; without light it is **like a limp balloon**. So in a way the *kli* is the main thing, and the *kavanos* are *davka* in it; but unfilled it is nothing, which is why the light is the main thing.

reviewQuestions.question: If a vessel comes from the thickening of the light, why is anything left "like a body without a soul" when the light goes?
What does one aim at in the Name *Havaya*, and why does the light then come by itself?
Why are the *Arizal*'s *kavanos* on the vessels of *Zeir Anpin* not *avoda zara*, and what do the fundraisers and the three prayers show?
How does "You are hidden" show where the hiding in the vessels is?
What are the three levels of the heart and of the liver, and how do sleep and the fetal position fit them?
If the vessels are the main thing, why does the text say "without a soul"?

notes.text: Line 7's second phrase ("because the man runs after the woman") cites his rendering at 044 w3018-3024, said when he returns to the line after the long discussion of kavanos; at the first reading (w762-776) he translates only the first half.

Class 044 from w864 on, and the opening of class 045 (w0-326), never read another line: the Hashem question, the upper Names, the avoda zara question, the fundraiser mashal, the vowel points and the three prayers all follow line 7, so they sit under it. Class 045 rereads the end of line 7 at w327-334, in a wording the transcript renders as "התקשרות וכולי".

The friend used as the example (044 w686-761, and 045 w605-619) is named in class ("Shmueli", as in chapter 29; and a student, "Ami", in the fundraiser mashal at 044 w2417-2908). Per STYLE.md they are "a friend we all know", "a friend" and "the listener". The person at home who asks whom he talked to (044 w2454) is his wife, and the doctor he learned the liver with (045 w3139-3203) is his wife too; neither is named in the text. "If I call you Boobie" (044 w1096) is written as "a nickname".

The source of the list of vowel points (044 w3071-3083: a listener asks "what book is that from?" and the answer is transcribed as "הפלאה שבחכמה") is unclear, and it is not clear who read the list; the block gives the list without a source. In the exchange that follows (w3084-3124) the transcript has both "kamatz is gevura, patach chesed" and "kamatz is chesed and patach gevura"; the question block gives the listener's version and his answer (different systems; kamatz is a fist, tzimtzum).

044 w3673-3695: "it's like it says by the angels, you to Avraham Avinu, you don't say no" is garbled; the block keeps only "you don't say no to him". 044 w3939-3982 ("songs like Rabbi Zaltsman, they go to the Rozovskys") is unclear; the block keeps only that upstairs one must know the letters, vowels, cantillation, crowns and tags.

044 w1561-1587: the Kohen Gadol of the Ten Martyrs is "what's-his-name" in class (it is Rabbi Yishmael Kohen Gadol); the block says "the Kohen Gadol". "The Tannaim" (w1536) is written "the sages of the Mishna".

045 w2412: he reads the total as "עולה רמ״ח" where the line has רמ"ג (243); the block follows the line (243, and with five more 248). Other readings differ from the line in small ways: line 32 הטבעת read as הדפקת (he explains it as breathing faster or slower; the block says only that through it the middos reach the body), line 45 הולד/ברכיו read as עובד/ירכיו, line 56 שקיו דאילנא read as "שכיח דילנו" (not translated).

Line 41 ("the inner divides") is explained twice: in its place he reads it as "the liver divides between the two systems" (045 w2173-2189), and after finishing the chapter he goes back to it (w2989-3301) on the liver as a sieve and intermediary; those three blocks are under lines 40-41 with outOfPlace. His physiology there is given with his own hesitation ("I think", "I don't know the exact physical thing").

Many lines of class 045 are read in Hebrew without English (lines 8, 10-11, 13-17, 19, 22-24, 27, 29-31, 33, 35, 38-43, 46-49, 51-54); their phrases have Hebrew only. Line 61's "it'll be like a limp balloon" and line 32's "he'll start breathing faster or slower" are his glosses given as he reads the words, used as the phrases' English.
Two blocks are flagged crude only for a word ("a nut", of himself in the fundraiser story; the "yo mama" graffiti). Neither is a teaching; both are delivery.
